extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, and readers interested in research integrity and clinical trial conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the validity, implementation, reporting, and consequences of randomization and allocation procedures in clinical trials, and deciding whether corrections or retraction are warranted. Focus is on trials where emergency-response teams were randomized by period/block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation scheme and allocation ratio match reported plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should accurately reflect the randomisation scheme and allocation ratio specified in the protocol (the page references concerns that the randomisation scheme and allocation ratio did not occur in the same ratio the authors had specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: authors stated a 1:2 allocation ratio (twice as many people in the intravenous group), but the observed data showed roughly equal group sizes. If observed allocation departs substantially from the planned ratio, this should prompt scrutiny and explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation implemented consistently in practice (no periods without randomisation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomisation must have been applied consistently during the trial; the article notes 'periods with no randomization, where all teams were assigned the same mode of treatment, and periods with an equal ratio of treatments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: block/period assignments that result in whole periods where one treatment was used exclusively, suggesting manual or operational deviations from the randomisation procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript must provide the correct description of how randomisation was performed
rubrics_metrics.description: The correct description of the randomization should be provided in the manuscript (Andersen wrote: 'The correct description of the randomization should be provided in the manuscript').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If implementation differed from the plan, authors should transparently describe the actual procedure used, including any deviations, manual processes, and their timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observed patient allocations should be statistically plausible under the planned randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: The numbers of patients in each treatment group should be consistent with the planned allocation; highly unlikely distributions (e.g., equal numbers when 1:2 was planned) indicate possible errors or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/statistical reviewers should assess whether the observed distribution is extremely unlikely to occur by chance and whether that undermines the trial's validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate recording of treatment given to each patient
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment actually given to each patient must be correctly recorded; concerns were raised whether 'the treatment given to each patient was correctly recorded' and that incorrect recording could render the study unsalvageable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If treatment assignment recording is unreliable, results and conclusions cannot be trusted. Investigations should verify source records and entry processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide convincing explanations for discrepancies (not speculative or weak)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations for unexpected discrepancies (e.g., COVID-19 pandemic effects, prolonged pre-hospital time) must be convincing; the authors' suggested explanations were described as 'not strongly convincing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weak or speculative rationales should prompt further audit or corrective action rather than acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate block structure and interchangeability of randomisation units (teams/weeks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the randomisation units (e.g., teams, weeks) and any block structure were handled appropriately; commenters noted a 'very clear block structure' and questioned interchangeability of teams or weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether blocks were balanced as intended and whether non-interchangeability could bias results; consider cluster-level effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider selection/reporting bias in case inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the decision to report a case was independent of treatment condition; one comment suggested 'the decision to report on a case was not independent of the treatment condition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If case inclusion depended on treatment, outcome reporting may be biased; audit inclusion criteria and reporting processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustive re-examination of data when concerns are raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should conduct a thorough re-examination of the data when substantive concerns are raised (authors 'launched an exhaustive one-month re-examination' of the data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-examination should document methods, findings, and whether deviations materially affect conclusions; independent oversight or audit may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction, replacement, or correction when errors threaten validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should consider retraction, replacement, or correction if errors are serious enough to bias conclusions; in this case the journal retracted the article and the authors requested retraction and replacement or a correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction can be appropriate even without evidence of misconduct if procedural errors undermine the integrity of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction does not necessarily imply ethical lapses or misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial statements may clarify that retraction 'in no way implies any ethical lapses or misconduct' when errors are judged unintentional procedural mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between honest error and misconduct in notices; such distinctions inform next steps (correction vs. investigation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of statistical review in identifying implementation flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical reviewers can identify discrepancies in randomisation and allocation (the concern was raised by Lars Andersen, a statistical reviewer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statistical review for trials to verify randomisation scheme, allocation ratios, and plausibility of observed data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and responsiveness to post-publication comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals and authors should transparently respond to online comments and extended criticisms (the retraction notice references an online comment and the authors provided responses and further explanations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, detailed engagement with post-publication critique supports integrity; failure to respond or opaque responses may worsen distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider operational disruptions (e.g., pandemics) as possible but insufficient sole explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic may affect adherence to procedures, but they do not automatically excuse large procedural deviations ('most of which occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should document how disruptions affected conduct and provide evidence that deviations do not invalidate findings; unexplained deviations require stronger corrective actions.
